stories.headline: US and Iran Exchange Maritime Attacks as Oil Prices Surge Past $100
stories.body:
The United States and Israel launched a military conflict against Iran on February 28, 2026 [c5]. US President Donald Trump said the war against Iran will end immediately after the upcoming US midterm elections [c1]. Trump claimed Iran is stalling an end to the war [c2]. He said Iran wants to secure a more favorable political environment in the US ahead of the midterms [c2].

A poll conducted in August 2026 showed that only 31 percent of Americans support the war in Iran [c4]. Support was down from 37 percent in March 2026 [c4]. US Energy Secretary Chris Wright spoke about future actions [c3]. Wright said the US may continue strikes against Iranian nuclear infrastructure instead of reaching a nuclear deal [c3].

Trump said that the US military has knocked out about nine Iranian oil tankers [c10]. US Central Command gave more details on these actions [c13]. Central Command said its strikes destroyed four Iranian tankers in the Gulf of Oman [c13]. These four ships were named Kaviz, Charminar, Horizon 1, and Riesco [c13]. Central Command said a fifth Iranian tanker named Derya was destroyed near Kharg Island [c13].

Iran said that it attacked 10 ships near the Strait of Hormuz [c6]. Iran said it launched these attacks after the US military sank five Iranian oil tankers [c6]. An attack occurred on an oil products tanker named Hercules Star off Dubai [c8]. One seafarer was killed aboard the ship [c8]. Another seafarer was reported missing after the attack [c8].

The Iranian Revolutionary Guards made a warning against further attacks [c9]. They said that they would hit 20 targets if their enemy struck two or three targets [c9]. Revolutionary Guard spokesman Hossein Mohebi announced plans to mark a new prohibited zone [c15]. Mohebi said Iran will set coordinates for this zone [c15]. The new prohibited zone will cover parts of the Sea of Oman and the Arabian Sea [c15].

Jordan's armed forces reported intercepting 20 Iranian missiles [c14]. These missiles were aimed at Muwaffaq Salti Air Base [c14]. Jordan reported no casualties from the missile interception [c14].

Energy markets saw sharp price rises during the military actions [c7, c11]. Benchmark Brent crude futures breached $100 a barrel [c7]. This was the first time Brent crude passed $100 since July 2026 [c7]. The Dutch benchmark gas contract rose by almost 4% to €78.73 a megawatt hour [c11]. This reached its highest level since January 2023 [c11]. China's crude oil imports recovered to nearly 9 million barrels per day in August 2026 [c12]. That figure was up from 7.15 million barrels per day in June [c12].

vocab.meaning: a person who works or travels on a ship
stopping or catching something before it reaches its target
forbidden or not allowed by authority

stories.headline: Apple Unveils Foldable iPhone Duo and iPhone 18 Pro Series
stories.body:
Apple unveiled its first foldable smartphone named the iPhone Duo at a starting price of $1,999 [c16]. The device opens into a horizontal 7.6-inch-wide screen [c17]. Apple made the iPhone Duo an eSIM-only device globally by completely removing the physical SIM tray [c21]. The iPhone Duo omits Face ID and uses a Touch ID sensor in the power button [c23]. Apple claims the phone offers up to 31 hours of video playback on its inner display [c22]. It offers up to 44 hours on its outer display [c22].

In India, the iPhone Duo starts at Rs 2,99,900 for the 256GB model [c29]. The 2TB model costs up to Rs 4,49,900 [c29]. Apple also raised the base price of the standard iPhone 17 in India to Rs 99,900 [c19]. It increased the ultra-thin iPhone Air price by Rs 30,000 to Rs 1,49,900 [c20].

Apple announced pre-orders for the iPhone 18 Pro and 18 Pro Max begin on September 12, 2026 [c18]. Stores will have them on September 18, 2026 [c18]. The 18 Pro starts at Rs 1,64,900 in India [c26]. The 18 Pro Max starts at Rs 1,79,900 [c26]. The 18 Pro series runs on an A20 Pro 2-nanometer processor [c28]. It includes Apple Reference Image to verify photo authenticity [c27].

Apple also introduced the Apple Watch Series 12 and Apple Watch Ultra 4 [c24]. Both watches run on the new S11 processor [c24]. They feature native daily tracking called Readiness score [c25].

vocab.meaning: able to be bent over on itself
the quality of being real or genuine
fixed firmly into a surrounding mass

stories.headline: IAEA Board Reports Iran to UN Security Council Over Nuclear Obligations
stories.body:
The International Atomic Energy Agency Board of Governors reported Iran to the UN Security Council for nuclear non-compliance [c30]. This resolution marks the first time in 20 years that the 35-member board has reported Iran [c32]. The United Kingdom, France, Germany, and the United States submitted the resolution together [c35]. Twenty-three countries voted in favor of the measure [c31]. Russia, China, and Niger voted against it [c31].

The IAEA suspects Iran holds about 400 kilograms of highly enriched uranium [c33]. That amount could produce 10 nuclear weapons if enriched further [c33]. Senior US officials said Iran had about 440 kilograms of 60% enriched uranium when the latest conflict started [c37].

Iran's mission to the UN said the non-compliance was caused entirely by aggression from the US and Israel [c34]. Iranian Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi said US and Israeli attacks disrupted nuclear inspections [c36]. He said those attacks were then used as a pretext for the resolution [c36]. Iran circulated an 11-page document warning Western nations not to turn the IAEA into a tool of war [c39]. China, Russia, and Iran said the vote risks politicizing a technical matter [c38]. US President Donald Trump said the US may soon hit the Pickaxe facility south of Natanz [c40].

vocab.meaning: a false reason given to hide the real reason
processed to increase the proportion of a specific element
making something into a political issue

stories.headline: Twelve Nations Impose Trade Sanctions on West Bank Israeli Settlements
stories.body:
Twelve countries coordinated new sanctions targeting trade with Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank [c45]. The coalition includes Britain, France, and Canada [c45]. UK Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband announced the British trade sanctions on the settlements [c42]. UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham defended the new trade ban [c41]. Last year, exports from occupied territories to the UK totaled $45 million out of $4.4 billion in total trade [c47].

UK Chief Rabbi Sir Ephraim Mirvis condemned the sanctions as a dark day for British Jews [c43]. But prominent British rabbis Jonathan Wittenberg and Alexandra Wright publicly supported the sanctions [c44]. Former Israeli Prime Minister Ehud Olmert and former military chief Dan Halutz signed a statement welcoming the UK measures [c46]. A poll showed nearly three-quarters of Jewish Israelis support partial or total annexation of the West Bank [c48].

Miliband said Israeli intelligence promised that intelligence sharing with the UK will continue unchanged [c49]. US President Donald Trump said he will speak to Israel about the sanctions [c50]. The UK government also announced fresh nuclear-related sanctions against Iranian ships [c51].

vocab.meaning: taking control of a territory and adding it to a country
penalties applied to a country or group to force compliance

stories.headline: Republicans Open Midterm Convention in Dallas With Trump as Speaker
stories.body:
Republican National Committee Chair Joe Gruters opened the party's two-day midterm convention in Dallas, Texas [c52]. The gathering at the American Airlines Center is the first midterm convention held by the Republican Party [c56]. US President Donald Trump is set as the main speaker for both nights [c60]. Before Trump left for Dallas, an emergency inflatable slide on Air Force One deployed by accident [c55].

The pro-Trump Super PAC Maga Inc holds a $400 million fund [c53]. It set aside $47 million for seven competitive midterm races [c53]. The convention schedule contains 109 items, including a segment on the 25th anniversary of the 9/11 attacks [c59]. It leaves out any segment on the ongoing war with Iran [c59].

A Reuters/Ipsos poll showed Trump with an approval rating of 33 percent [c57]. Another poll by FT/Focaldata found that 57 percent of respondents feel their personal finances got worse after Trump took office [c58]. In Missouri, legal challengers filed an emergency appeal with the US Supreme Court [c54]. They are fighting a federal judge's order that forces Missouri to use a new Republican-drawn map in the midterms [c54].

vocab.meaning: redrawing the boundaries of political voting areas
a main speech given at a major event

stories.headline: German Chancellor Merz Cancels Trump Call After Far-Right Election Victory
stories.body:
German Chancellor Friedrich Merz cancelled a planned phone call with US President Donald Trump [c64]. Merz took the action after Trump praised a far-right election victory in Germany [c64]. Trump posted on Truth Social to celebrate the win by the Alternative für Deutschland party, ending his message with MGGA [c65].

The AfD won 43.8% of the vote in the Saxony-Anhalt state election on September 6 [c61]. The result left the AfD three seats short of an absolute majority [c71]. The Christian Democratic Union saw its vote share fall to 17.2%, down from 37.1% in 2021 [c62]. Voter turnout reached nearly 78% [c63].

In a parliament debate, Merz accused the AfD of seeking ethnic cleansing [c66]. He said one in six skilled workers in Germany has a migration background [c68]. Merz also criticized the AfD for not condemning a drone attack at Leipzig airport linked to Russia [c72]. AfD co-leader Alice Weidel said Merz's coalition had failed and his time as chancellor was up [c70]. Bundestag President Julia Klöckner threatened to expel shouting AfD lawmakers [c69]. In Serbia, President Aleksandar Vučić dissolved parliament for snap elections in October 2026 [c67].

vocab.meaning: to force someone to leave a place or organization
a temporary alliance of political parties forming a government

stories.headline: Delhi Inspects PG Hostels After Fatal Satya Niketan Building Collapse
stories.body:
Seven people died when a five-storey building collapsed in Delhi's Satya Niketan area on September 6 [c79]. Work done 10 days before the collapse put about three truckloads of debris into the basement [c77]. On the day of the collapse, workers removed a ground-floor wall to expand a shop [c78]. Police arrested labor contractor Sanoj Kumar for supervising the renovation [c80]. Police also arrested PG operator Sudhanshu, while his associate Shubham Tyagi remained on the run [c85]. Property owners Hariram Bansal and Urmila Gupta were sent to 14 days of judicial custody [c86].

Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta ordered the demolition of an adjoining dilapidated building [c87]. The Municipal Corporation of Delhi then inspected 1,252 paying guest accommodation buildings [c73]. Officials found 1,201 safe, 39 needing minor repairs, nine needing major repairs, and three dangerous [c74]. The agency also picked 26 tall structures above four upper floors for close monitoring [c75].

Student activists reported mobile internet slowdowns in the area and claimed jammers were used [c82]. Delhi Police denied the claim and said networks were operational [c83]. Meanwhile, India's Supreme Court agreed to review compliance rules for illegal PG structures across the country [c88].

vocab.meaning: in a state of disrepair or ruin as a result of age or neglect
arrested or caught by authority

stories.headline: India Prepares to Host 18th BRICS Summit in New Delhi
stories.body:
India is hosting the 18th BRICS Summit on September 12 and 13, 2026, in New Delhi [c89]. The event takes place at Bharat Mandapam [c89]. The official theme for the summit is Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability [c97]. Prime Minister Narendra Modi will host a gala dinner for participating leaders on Saturday evening [c90].

Modi has planned key two-way talks with international leaders during the summit [c91, c92]. He is scheduled to hold a meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin on Friday [c92]. On Saturday, Modi is scheduled to hold a formal meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping [c91].

Economic discussions between India and Russia are also taking place alongside the summit preparations [c93, c95]. Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal will meet Russian counterpart Anton Alikhanov on Thursday [c93]. Their meeting takes place at the INNOPROM India 2026 industrial trade fair [c93]. The trade fair runs at Bharat Mandapam from September 9 to 11 [c95]. India and Russia have set a target to reach $100 billion in bilateral trade by 2030 [c94]. That amount equals approximately Rs 9.45 lakh crore [c94].

India is also developing its internal trade networks [c96]. The National Industrial Corridor Development Programme covers 11 industrial corridors [c96]. It includes 20 greenfield industrial smart cities spread across 13 Indian states [c96].

The BRICS group has grown significantly since its founding [c98, c99]. It started as the BRIC alliance between Brazil, Russia, India, and China in 2006 [c98]. The group held its first summit in Yekaterinburg in 2009 [c98]. South Africa joined the group in 2011 [c98]. BRICS expanded to 11 full member states in recent years [c99]. It admitted Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran, Saudi Arabia, and the United Arab Emirates in January 2024 [c99]. Indonesia joined as a full member in January 2025 [c99].

Authorities in New Delhi have put detailed security and traffic measures in place for the summit [c100, c101]. Delhi Traffic Police set up 22 diversion points across the city [c100]. They are regulating traffic on more than 35 roads [c100]. Roadside parking within 200 meters of controlled roads is strictly forbidden [c101]. But Delhi Metro operations will run normally without any disruption across all stations [c102].

Air travel infrastructure has also been expanded for summit guests [c103, c104]. Delhi International Airport Limited opened Pier C at Terminal 3 on the night of September 9 [c103]. The airport created dedicated immigration counters for summit participants [c104]. It also made special arrangements for airplane landing and parking [c104].

vocab.meaning: involving two parties or countries
a temporary rerouting of traffic
relating to previously undeveloped land used for new projects
